competition_series.note: Confirmed by Adam: COSA, COSTA and Ladies COFTA are three separate competitions, not one renamed series.

competition_full_names.note: What each acronym stands for, organiser-confirmed 2026-08-21. CONAFA, COSTA and COSA are each their own association despite the similar names. Ladies COFTA is COFTA's women's competition and shares its name exactly. The Ark Cup is not an acronym and has no association name recorded, so it names its diocese instead rather than borrowing another competition's.

competition_dioceses.note: Organiser-confirmed 2026-08-21: CONAFA is played in the Diocese of the Midlands, and every London-based competition in the Diocese of London.

merge_guards.title: The two St Mina clubs
merge_guards.rule: Two distinct clubs carrying IDENTICAL church names, differing only by city - the same shape as G1's Nottingham/East London pair. merge_guards.title: The two St Mark clubs
merge_guards.rule: A third name collision alongside G1. St Mark, Kensington won CONAFA 2014 and COFTA 2009; St Mary & St Mark, Birmingham appear in CONAFA 2015 and in COFTA 2017's joint entrant with Rotherham. A prefix or token match on 'St Mark' would merge them. Never.

conflict_register.note: Every item here is an internal inconsistency in the source material or an identity question that cannot be resolved from the sources. Claude Code must NOT silently resolve any of these. Store the data as flagged, and surface the flag in the admin view.

data_conflicts.issue: Published goalscorer leaderboard exceeds event-derived counts.
data_conflicts.detail: Daniel Samaan published 5 / events 4; Stavros Akriviadis published 5 / events 4; Robel Hailemichael published 2 / events 1. Possible cause: shootout conversions in the Brighton v Stevenage semi-final counted as goals in the app leaderboard. Unconfirmed.
data_conflicts.resolution: Store both figures. Do not pick one.

data_conflicts.detail: Golders Green 2-0 St Mary's shows three Golders Green goal events (Marino Rofail, CJ Forbes, Andrew Louis) against an official 2-0.
data_conflicts.resolution: Preserve the official 2-0. Store all three events flagged.

data_conflicts.detail: The published table gives Mariam Makkar 4 WOTM and totals 8 awards across 7 matches. Per-match records give Makkar 3 (Games 1, 2, Final).
data_conflicts.resolution: Store per-match awards as primary; store the published table flagged.

data_conflicts.issue: Source's own count of unattributed goals is wrong and self-contradictory.
data_conflicts.detail: The summary page says 'three goals have no displayed scorer'; the goalscorer table note says 'two goals are unassigned' then describes four. Arithmetic against the fixtures gives 35 total goals and 31 recorded scorers, i.e. FOUR unattributed: 2 in Archangel Michael 0-2 St Anthony, 1 in the Brighton 1-0 St Mark semi-final, 1 for St George in the final.
data_conflicts.resolution: Record four unattributed goals. Do not reproduce the source's counts.

data_conflicts.issue: Final home/away orientation conflicts within the source.
data_conflicts.detail: Two places render it 'Archangel Michael, Golders Green 0-1 Anba Abraam, Brighton'; one renders it 'Anba Abraam, Brighton 1-0 Archangel Michael, Golders Green'. Result is identical either way.
data_conflicts.resolution: Majority orientation stored (Golders Green home). Flag for confirmation.

data_conflicts.issue: Three Group B matches display goals with no team attribution.
data_conflicts.detail: B-R1 Brighton 2-1 St Mark (3 goals: Demas Ramsis, Steven Sava, Sydney Noulton); B-R3 Brighton 2-1 Archangel Michael (Demas Ramsis, Sebastian, Ebi Abdel-Malek); B-R4 Brighton 3-1 St Mark (Stefano, Stavros Akriviadis, Abanoub Fakhoury, Leon Lawandi). Which scorer belongs to the losing side is not determinable.
data_conflicts.resolution: Store scorers with team = null and a flag. Do NOT infer from squad history in other editions.

data_conflicts.issue: One goal in the dataset did not come from the source app.
data_conflicts.detail: Nduoma Chilaka in Nottingham 1-0 Rotherham (A-R6-02) was supplied by the tournament organiser. Minute unknown.

data_conflicts.issue: A published source calls COFTA 2014 'the 10th annual' tournament; Adam's chronology makes it the 9th.
data_conflicts.detail: The 2014 blog describes that year's tournament as the 10th annual. Adam's roll gives a first edition in 2005 and NO tournament in 2013, which makes 2014 the ninth: 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2014. The published claim would require either a pre-2005 start or a tournament in 2013.
data_conflicts.resolution: Adam's chronology is canonical and is what the archive stores. The published claim is recorded here as a source discrepancy. UNRESOLVED and non-blocking - it changes no stored value, and may simply be the source counting inclusively or forgetting the missing year.

resolved.answer: SMPK and Pope Kyrillos, Hounslow are the same club. Merged as 'St Mary & Pope Kyrillos VI, Hounslow'. The CONAFA 2025 'St Demiana and Pope Kyrillos VI' entry is the WORTHING club, a separate entity that also carries Pope Kyrillos VI in its name. These two must never be merged.

The Ark Cup 2026 'St Mary's' is Golders Green's second team. Recorded as 'Archangel Michael, Golders Green B' with per-edition display name "St Mary's". The Ark Cup host church is therefore Golders Green.
All St Mark / St Marks / St Mark's entries are St Mark, Kensington. Merged.

COFTA 2014 top scorer spelling, 2026-08-21. Adam's 'Nduoma Chilaka' is canonical. The published 2014 report prints 'Chilaki'. The report spelling is preserved as a player_name_variant and as the award row's source string; player_canonical is 'Nduoma Chilaka'. Not a conflict - a ruling.

COSTA CORRECTIONS, 2026-08-21. Two things Adam corrected after the backfill. (1) COSTA stands for Coptic Orthodox SOUTHERN Tournament Association, not Soccer - the earlier expansion recorded on 2026-08-21 was wrong and is superseded. (2) COSTA began in 2022, so costa-2022 IS the inaugural edition. The origins_unrecorded note that 0026 put on every COSTA edition existed precisely to stop the earliest archived row being read as the first tournament played; that guard is now obsolete and 0031 removes it. 'COSTA founding year' is struck from records_being_sought.

CONAFA 2018 and 2019, 2026-08-21. Adam first wrote that Brighton won 2018 and 2019 in a sentence about COSTA, then corrected it within the minute to CONAFA. The correction is the record: two CONAFA editions are added, champion Brighton, minimal confidence, nothing else known. COSTA gains nothing from this - it did not exist in 2018. Adam separately believes there was no CONAFA in 2020, 2021 or 2022; that is held as a belief in no_tournament_years, not as a confirmed absence. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24 by C16: CONAFA did not run in 2018-2022 at all, and both edition rows this entry created have been removed.

CONAFA 2018 AND 2019 REMOVED, 2026-08-24. This reverses a decision taken three days earlier and is the only place in the archive where Adam has contradicted Adam, so it is recorded in full. On 2026-08-21 Adam wrote 'Brighton won 2018 and 2019' in a sentence about COSTA, then corrected it within the minute to CONAFA; migration 0032 duly created conafa-2018 and conafa-2019 with Brighton as champion and nothing else known. On 2026-08-24 he confirmed that CONAFA did not run at all between 2017 and 2023 - a five-year gap. The later statement wins, and three things support it over the earlier one. It is specific rather than a one-line self-correction: it names the gap, its length, and the resumption year. It is consistent with the surrounding rows, 2017 (Manchester) running straight into 2023. And the earlier claim is fully explained as a misattribution, because COFTA 2018 and COFTA 2019 BOTH already record Brighton as champion - 'Brighton won 2018 and 2019' was already true, of the wrong competition. Brighton's CONAFA titles go from seven to five. No other row is touched.

COFTA 2010 DATES, 2026-08-24. The archive held 10-12 September 2010; the official report gives 11-12 September. The report is a contemporaneous document and is taken as correct, so the row now reads 11-12 September. Non-blocking, and logged rather than silently overwritten because the earlier range was itself organiser-supplied. If the three-day range was right, this is the entry that says where the two-day one came from.

NDUOMA CHILAKA'S 2014 TALLY vs THE OWN-GOAL CORRECTION, 2026-08-24. The archive records 5 goals, organiser-confirmed, and 0028 made that figure the record rather than a published-summary figure. The 2014 report describes the final's free-kick as going in off the goalkeeper's heel and being AWARDED AS AN OWN GOAL - explicitly not his. It also attributes only two of his goals in so many words, the pair of headers in the 2-2 with Croydon. There is no goal-by-goal record for 2014, so the archive CANNOT determine whether the 5 ever included that own goal. The 5 therefore stands untouched and is NOT recomputed; the own goal is stored separately, credited to Nottingham and conceded by Brighton, with no player. What this entry exists to prevent is someone later reading the own goal as a sixth Chilaka goal, or quietly reducing the 5 to 4 to make the arithmetic close. Neither is supported.

THE 2006-2010 SOUTHERN-CHAMPIONS CLAIM RECONCILES - CORROBORATION, NOT CONFLICT, 2026-08-24. The COFTA 2010 report states that each southern church had won COFTA once in the previous five years. Adam confirms St Mark counts as southern. Reading 2006 to 2010 against the confirmed roll: Croydon 2006, Golders Green 2007, Stevenage 2008, St Mark 2009, Brighton 2010 - five different southern clubs, one title each, no repeats. It reconciles exactly. This is deliberately NOT logged as a conflict: it is an independent contemporaneous source agreeing with the organiser's roll, and it is the second thing to corroborate the newly filled 2007 and 2008 champions.

'HELD THE TROPHY 4 YEARS' IN THE 2014 REPORT, 2026-08-24. The report frames Brighton as having held the trophy for four years, which reads as 2010-2013. The confirmed roll has Brighton winning 2010, 2011 and 2012 - three titles - and no tournament at all in 2013. Both are true of a fashion: they held it for four calendar years precisely BECAUSE 2013 was not played, so nobody took it off them. Minor, non-blocking, and the roll is not altered. Logged so the discrepancy is not rediscovered as a missing 2013 title.
